messages:
leah: Heads-up — we just noticed a tiny 10m window (2026-03-20 22:00–22:10 UTC) that never made it into the hourly aggregates. Thinking about running micro reprocess jobs (micro-catchups) instead of the usual full backfill. pros/cons? :eyes:

sam: Do we know the event volume for that window? if it's tiny we can do delta-only and avoid huge cost. also watch quotas. :money_with_wings:

leah: Volume ~ 48k events across prod, but high-value routes for a couple of tenants. rough cost estimate looks small-ish but uncertain because of current aggregators charging per-record in the replayer path.

priya: If we have a delta-only path in the internal replay API that does prefix/KV-aware stitches, we can avoid re-running entire aggregators. We debated this last quarter. Should we expose that API for operators?

mike: From a console UX POV we should show an estimated cost + ETA for micro-catchups inline before triggering. Right now console only shows full-backfill estimates which scare users. tiny toggle: "only affected windows" vs "full shard replay".

joan: Agree on the toggle. Also we need to ensure the micro-jobs won't get preempted by reserved capacity policies. Small jobs still count against tenant slot quotas — otherwise they'll fail mid-run and produce partial aggregates.

tim: For ops, here's a dry-run command I used earlier in staging that exercises delta path:```bash
replayer --mode=delta-only --start=2026-03-20T22:00:00Z --end=2026-03-20T22:10:00Z --tenant=acme --shard=04 --dry-run
```That prints estimated token reads and output row count.

priya: If we expose delta-only, we need strong contract: idempotency + "catchup_reason" metadata tag so downstream QA and cost accounting can filter these runs. Suggest tag: `catchup_reason=late_ingest_small_window`.

leah: Good call on tags. Also: ops-bot, can you run a low-priority dry-run and return the estimator numbers? want to validate cost gauge before we surface UI toggle.

ops-bot: deploybot: queued replayer dry-run (delta-only) for window 2026-03-20T22:00Z-22:10Z on prod-sim cluster. job id: job-20260320-510. ETA ~30s.

ops-bot: deploybot: dry-run complete. estimator output: {rows: "~1.9k", token_reads: "~120k", est_cost_usd: "0.34", peak_mem_mb: "620"} (printed from staging estimator).

sam: 0.34 looks fine. main risk is quota exhaustion if multiple micro-catchups run concurrently. We need a console guard that groups small windows into a single "micro-batch" with concurrency cap.

mike: UX idea: when a user selects multiple adjacent tiny windows, auto-group into a single micro-batch and show a slider for concurrency (1–4). default 1. include "expected completion" and "estimated cost".

joan: Ops requirements: micro-batch scheduler must respect reserved capacity lanes and fallback to host-level fallback policy (route to lower-priority pool) instead of failing. Also, record preemption events in telemetry so we can alert if >5% fail.

priya: API debate: do we implement this as a new Replayer endpoint `/v2/replay/delta` or add a query param to the existing `/v1/replay`? I lean v2 because delta requires different guarantees (kv-stitch, idempotency semantics).

tim: v2 makes sense. We can route v2 to specialized worker pool optimized for small-window latency and cheaper kernel choices. That avoids contention with large batch jobs.

leah: Okay. Next steps: 1) ops run a non-prod full-dry-run for several sample tenants and post estimator outputs (sam/tim) 2) product/ux (mike) mock console toggle + grouping behavior 3) platform (priya) spec for /v2/replay/delta + tagging contract 4) SRE (joan) define scheduler preemption policy and alerts. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow.

sam: +1. I'll also add a quick quota check to the estimator so UI can disable the toggle if it would breach concurrent quota.

mike: I'll throw an initial mockup into Figma and link it here when ready. https://go.redwood/ux/micro-catchup-mock

priya: small ops note — we should also add a safety "max-affected-tenants" cap to prevent single-tenant spikes from creating lots of tiny jobs. maybe a default of 3 tenants per micro-batch.

joan: +1 on cap. also we should append `catchup_reason` to emitted telemetry events for better billing attribution. ops will pick filter query to surface failures.

leah: perfect. thanks team. I'll make the sync invite and add an agenda (dry-run results + API spec + UX mock).
